# Auth Barrier Checklist: P-RF03 — Biometric authentication vault

**Purpose**: Validate requirements quality for the three dimensions where this unit carries the most risk — the on-device security boundary (FR-002/FR-014/FR-015), lifecycle/timing of the lock (FR-001/FR-007–FR-010), and failure/fallback paths (FR-004/FR-006/FR-012, Edge Cases) — before `/speckit-tasks` turns spec.md into implementation work.
**Created**: 2026-10-11
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Security & On-Device Boundary

- [ ] CHK001 Is "entirely on-device" for authentication (FR-002) specific enough to rule out any transient transmission of the PIN value or raw biometric data, even for logging/telemetry purposes? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK002 Does the spec define what "the single typed-failure network call path already established by the foundation unit" (FR-014) means precisely enough that it cannot be read as permitting a new ad hoc HTTP call? [Clarity, Spec §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK003 Is it specified that passing the local barrier must never be treated as equivalent to backend authentication (FR-015) in every call site that checks "is the user authenticated"? [Completeness, Spec §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK004 Are the storage requirements for the Device PIN specified in a way that is testable for requirements quality purposes — e.g., "never transmitted to or validated by the backend" (Key Entities) — without mandating a specific hashing/storage mechanism that belongs in plan.md rather than spec.md? [Consistency, Spec §Key Entities]
- [ ] CHK005 Is there a requirement covering what happens if the device's secure storage for the PIN becomes unavailable or is cleared by the OS between sessions (distinct from "no PIN configured yet")? [Gap, Coverage]
- [ ] CHK006 Does the spec distinguish, for requirements purposes, between "biometrics preference" (an account flag written via the backend) and "the actual biometric check" (never backend-validated) clearly enough that a reader could not conflate the two? [Clarity, Spec §Key Entities]

## Lifecycle & Timing

- [ ] CHK007 Is the 5-minute background threshold specified with an unambiguous reference point (e.g., time of backgrounding vs. time of last unlock) so two readers could not compute different results from the same scenario? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-007, §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK008 Is "resume exactly the screen and state the user left" (FR-008) defined with enough specificity to be objectively verified (e.g., does "state" include scroll position, in-progress text input, modal visibility)? [Measurability, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK009 Is the requirement that the barrier appears "before the previously visible screen becomes visible or interactive" (FR-007) clear about whether the underlying screen may render behind the barrier (visually present but not interactive) or must not render at all? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK010 Does the spec define behavior for the boundary condition where the app is backgrounded multiple times within the 5-minute window (e.g., does each backgrounding reset the timer, or only the first)? [Gap, Edge Case]
- [ ] CHK011 Is the distinction between "app suspended in background" and "app process killed by the OS" (Edge Cases) specified with criteria an implementer could use to classify a given resume event, or does it assume platform-reported state the spec doesn't name? [Clarity, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK012 Is FR-009's "fixed value with no user-facing setting" requirement consistent with there being no other requirement or assumption elsewhere in the spec that implies configurability (e.g., via a future Settings screen)? [Consistency, Spec §FR-009, §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK013 Does the spec specify what happens to Vault Lock State (and the last-unlocked timestamp) across an app restart that is not itself a biometric/PIN prompt event (e.g., a crash-and-relaunch under 5 minutes)? [Gap, Edge Case]

## Failure & Fallback Paths

- [ ] CHK014 Is "a biometric attempt fails or is not recognized" (FR-004) specified broadly enough to clearly cover user-cancellation and OS-level dismissal as the same case as sensor misread, or does it leave room for a narrower reading that treats them differently? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK015 Is the "no limit that locks them out of the app entirely" requirement (User Story 2, Acceptance Scenario 3) reconciled with any implicit expectation of rate-limiting or lockout behavior that might be assumed from typical PIN-entry UX, so there's no conflict for an implementer to resolve on their own? [Consistency, Spec §User Story 2]
- [ ] CHK016 Does the spec define what, if anything, is logged or surfaced when repeated incorrect PIN attempts occur (e.g., is there a requirement for a soft warning before "usar e-mail e senha" is suggested more prominently), or is zero such behavior an explicit scope decision? [Gap, Assumption]
- [ ] CHK017 Is the exact error message text ("Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN", FR-004) specified as a requirement in a way consistent with how other user-facing strings are specified elsewhere in the spec (e.g., PIN mismatch message in FR-012 has no literal text given)? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004, §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK018 Is the fallback for "no biometric hardware or nothing enrolled at the OS level" (Edge Cases) specified identically for first-launch-ever-on-device vs. a device that previously had biometrics enabled and lost enrollment, or could these require different requirements that the spec doesn't separate? [Coverage, Edge Case]
- [ ] CHK019 Does the spec specify what the PIN entry screen shows immediately after the biometric prompt is dismissed/cancelled by the user (distinct from a failed scan) — is this covered by FR-004 or left ambiguous? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK020 Is the "usar e-mail e senha" escape hatch (FR-006) specified as available from every state of the vault screen (biometric prompt, PIN-after-failure, first-time PIN setup) or only from some, and if only some, is that scoping explicit? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006]

## First-Time PIN Setup Interplay

- [ ] CHK021 Is the requirement that an app kill mid-setup "resumes the PIN setup flow" (Edge Cases) specific enough about what state is resumed from (e.g., back to PIN entry step 1, or preserving the first-entered PIN for confirmation) to be implementable without guessing? [Clarity, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK022 Does the spec reconcile FR-013's "optionally enable Face ID/Touch ID... as part of first-time PIN setup" with the Clarifications answer that the `PATCH /account/settings` write is fire-and-forget — i.e., is it clear the user's biometric toggle takes effect locally regardless of that write's outcome? [Consistency, Spec §FR-013, §FR-014, §Clarifications]
- [ ] CHK023 Is there a requirement for what the user sees (if anything) when the fire-and-forget `biometricEnabled` write fails, or is "no synchronous retry, no blocking" (FR-014) explicitly understood to also mean no error UI at all? [Gap, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-014]

## Measurability & Traceability

- [ ] CHK024 Can SC-001's "100% of cold launches and background resumes... show the authentication barrier" be objectively measured given the requirements as written, or does it depend on an undefined instrumentation/observation method? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK025 Can SC-005's "screen state underneath... is unchanged in every observed case" be verified against a concrete, enumerated definition of "state" (scroll position, visible content) or does it rely on an open-ended notion of equivalence? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005]
- [ ] CHK026 Is a requirement & acceptance-criteria ID scheme established and consistently applied (FR-001…FR-018, SC-001…SC-005) such that every acceptance scenario can be traced to at least one FR? [Traceability]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK027 Is the assumption that "device biometric availability... is read from the platform's own biometrics API" (Assumptions) validated against FR-003's requirement to attempt biometrics first when available — i.e., is there a requirement for what happens if that platform API itself errors rather than returning a clean available/unavailable answer? [Gap, Assumption]
- [ ] CHK028 Is the dependency on F000's session machinery (FR-015, "silent renewal, or a full login if the session can no longer be renewed") specified with enough detail that a reader can tell which F000 component owns that decision, without this spec needing to redefine it? [Dependency, Spec §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK029 Is the assumption that the "Sessão expirada" overlay is "unaffected by this unit" (Assumptions) consistent with FR-001's requirement that the vault MUST gate every cold launch/resume — i.e., is there a documented reason the two don't collide when a session expires while the vault is also due to trigger? [Conflict, Consistency, Spec §Assumptions, §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK030 Is the assumption that no separate PIN-creation screen exists in the prototype, and that the same keypad component is reused for create-then-confirm (Assumptions), reconciled with FR-005's requirement describing PIN entry generically — does FR-005 as written clearly apply to both unlock-entry and setup-entry, or only to one? [Consistency, Spec §FR-005, §Assumptions]
